card.hypothesis: Sensor drift induces non-stationary noise that breaks conformal prediction's exchangeability assumption.
card.proposed_mechanism: Gradual baseline shift in sensor output changes signal mean, altering error distribution and causing miscalibrated intervals.
card.rival_explanation: Coverage failure stems from temporal autocorrelation violating exchangeability, not sensor drift.
card.rival_prediction: Coverage loss will be similar across sensors regardless of measured drift magnitude.
card.distinguishing_test: If coverage deficit correlates with sensor drift after adjusting for temperature and humidity, the mechanism is supported; otherwise the rival is supported.
card.effect_size_rationale: Sensor drift can produce substantial bias in physiological measurements, leading to large coverage errors.
card.testable_prediction: Segments with higher sensor drift will show lower coverage.
card.failure_condition: No association between sensor drift magnitude and coverage.
card.statistical_test_plan: Partial correlation between sensor drift magnitude and coverage deficit, controlling for temperature and humidity.
card.falsification_test: Perform sensor recalibration mid-experiment; if coverage improves to nominal after recalibration, the mechanism is supported; if coverage does not improve, it is falsified.

card.hypothesis: Arousal-induced heteroscedasticity in physiological signals leads to conformal prediction coverage instability.
card.proposed_mechanism: Increased arousal raises signal variance, widening prediction errors; conformal's assumption of homoscedastic error causes intervals to be too narrow during high arousal, producing under-coverage.
card.rival_explanation: Coverage instability arises from model misspecification (e.g., using linear relationships) rather than arousal-driven variance changes.
card.rival_prediction: Coverage deficits will be uniform across arousal levels if the model is misspecified.
card.distinguishing_test: If coverage deficit correlates with arousal after adjusting for time of day and caffeine, the mechanism is supported; if not, the rival is supported.
card.effect_size_rationale: Arousal is known to moderately affect variance of signals such as heart rate and skin conductance.
card.testable_prediction: Higher arousal will be associated with lower coverage (under-coverage).
card.failure_condition: No significant correlation between arousal level and coverage deficit.
card.statistical_test_plan: Regression of coverage deficit on arousal level with random intercept for subject, controlling for time of day and caffeine intake.
card.falsification_test: Induce a calm state via guided breathing and measure coverage; if coverage does not return to nominal, the mechanism is falsified.

card.hypothesis: Systematic labeling errors in the reference standard bias conformal prediction nonconformity scores, destabilizing coverage.
card.proposed_mechanism: Mislabelled events (e.g., false arrhythmia annotations) produce consistently high or low nonconformity scores, shifting the empirical quantile used for interval construction and causing over- or under-coverage.
card.rival_explanation: Coverage failure results from the algorithm's sensitivity to outliers, not from labeling errors.
card.rival_prediction: Segments with many outliers will show coverage loss regardless of label error rate.
card.distinguishing_test: If correcting label errors improves coverage while outlier removal does not, the mechanism is supported; if the opposite, the rival is supported.
card.effect_size_rationale: Label errors can drastically shift empirical quantiles, producing large coverage deviations.
card.testable_prediction: Segments with higher label disagreement will exhibit lower coverage.
card.failure_condition: No relationship between label disagreement rate and coverage.
card.statistical_test_plan: Logistic regression of coverage failure (binary) on proportion of disputed labels, adjusting for signal artifact rate.
card.falsification_test: Obtain blind re-annotations from an expert panel; if coverage reaches nominal using the corrected labels, the mechanism is supported; if coverage does not improve, it is falsified.

card.hypothesis: Failure to stratify conformal prediction by activity type leads to heterogeneous error distributions and unstable coverage.
card.proposed_mechanism: Different activities (e.g., walking vs resting) generate distinct signal dynamics; pooling violates exchangeability, causing activity-specific over- or under-coverage.
card.rival_explanation: Coverage instability stems from insufficient calibration set size rather than activity heterogeneity.
card.rival_prediction: Increasing the calibration set size will uniformly improve coverage across all activities.
card.distinguishing_test: If computing conformal separately for each activity restores nominal coverage, the mechanism is supported; if coverage remains off despite stratification, the rival is supported.
card.effect_size_rationale: Activity-related changes in signal statistics are moderate but sufficient to affect conformal quantiles.
card.testable_prediction: Coverage during walking will be lower than during rest when a single conformal model is used.
card.failure_condition: No difference in coverage between activity types.
card.statistical_test_plan: Compute coverage per activity and test difference using a chi-square test of proportions.
card.falsification_test: Apply activity-specific conformal calibration; if coverage becomes nominal across all activities, the mechanism is supported; if coverage remains off, it is falsified.

card.hypothesis: Heavy-tailed error distributions cause conformal prediction intervals to be too narrow in the tails, reducing coverage for extreme values.
card.proposed_mechanism: High kurtosis in prediction errors leads to underestimated tail mass; conformal's empirical quantile fails to capture extreme errors, resulting in under-coverage in the distribution tails.
card.rival_explanation: Coverage loss arises from using an inappropriate conformity score function (e.g., absolute error) rather than heavy tails.
card.rival_prediction: Switching to a different score (e.g., squared error) will fix coverage regardless of error kurtosis.
card.distinguishing_test: If using a robustness-oriented score (e.g., Huber loss) improves tail coverage, the mechanism is supported; if not, the rival is supported.
card.effect_size_rationale: Heavy tails may affect only extreme quantiles, producing modest changes in overall coverage.
card.testable_prediction: Segments with higher error kurtosis will show lower coverage in the 95% tails.
card.failure_condition: No difference in tail coverage between high and low kurtosis groups.
card.statistical_test_plan: Compare tail coverage between high vs low kurtosis groups using Welch's t-test.
card.falsification_test: Apply a heavy-tail aware conformal method (e.g., quantile regression forests); if coverage normalizes, the mechanism is supported; if coverage remains off, it is falsified.

card.hypothesis: Subject-specific medication alters both the mean and variance of physiological signals, leading to conformal prediction coverage instability.
card.proposed_mechanism: Medication (e.g., beta-blockers) reduces heart rate mean and variability, shifting error distribution and causing conformal intervals to be misaligned, producing either over- or under-coverage depending on direction.
card.rival_explanation: Coverage instability is due to time-varying noise unrelated to medication.
card.rival_prediction: Coverage deficits will be uncorrelated with medication status after accounting for time-varying noise.
card.distinguishing_test: If coverage differs between medicated and non-medicated subjects after controlling for age and underlying condition, the mechanism is supported; if not, the rival is supported.
card.effect_size_rationale: Medications like beta-blockers are known to produce moderate changes in heart rate mean and variance.
card.testable_prediction: Subjects taking medication will have coverage that deviates from nominal in a consistent direction (e.g., under-coverage for beta-blockers).
card.failure_condition: No significant difference in coverage between medicated and non-medicated groups.
card.statistical_test_plan: Two-sample t-test comparing coverage between medicated and non-medicated subjects, controlling for age and underlying condition via ANCOVA.
card.falsification_test: Withdraw medication in a crossover design; if coverage moves toward nominal, the mechanism is supported; if coverage does not change, it is falsified.

card.hypothesis: Class imbalance in the calibration set causes conformal prediction to produce intervals with systematically incorrect coverage for the minority class.
card.proposed_mechanism: When the calibration set under-represents a physiological state (e.g., arrhythmia), the empirical quantile used for interval width is dominated by the majority class, leading to intervals that are too narrow for the minority class and under-coverage.
card.rival_explanation: Coverage loss for minority class stems from the predictor's poor performance on that class, not from conformal calibration.
card.rival_prediction: Improving the predictor's accuracy on the minority class will fix coverage regardless of class imbalance.
card.distinguishing_test: If reweighting the calibration set to balance classes restores nominal coverage for the minority class while predictor accuracy unchanged, the mechanism is supported; if coverage does not improve, the rival is supported.
card.effect_size_rationale: Severe class imbalance can shift quantiles substantially, producing large coverage errors.
card.testable_prediction: Segments belonging to the minority class will exhibit lower coverage than those from the majority class when using a standard conformal predictor.
card.failure_condition: No difference in coverage between minority and majority class segments.
card.statistical_test_plan: Logistic regression of coverage failure (binary) on class membership, adjusting for signal noise level and feature distribution shift.
card.falsification_test: Apply class-weighted conformal prediction (e.g., weighted quantiles); if coverage for minority class reaches nominal, the mechanism is supported; if coverage remains low, it is falsified.

card.hypothesis: Using a fixed-parameter nonconformity score (e.g., absolute residual from a linear model) that does not adapt to amplitude scaling of physiological signals leads to miscalibrated intervals when signal gain changes across segments.
card.proposed_mechanism: Changes in signal gain (e.g., due to electrode contact) scale residuals proportionally, causing the nonconformity score distribution to shift; the fixed quantile threshold no longer matches the true error distribution.
card.rival_explanation: Coverage instability stems from non-linear relationships that the linear model cannot capture, not from gain changes.
card.rival_prediction: If a flexible model (e.g., neural net) is used, coverage will stabilize even with gain fluctuations.
card.distinguishing_test: Switching to a gain-invariant score (e.g., normalized residual) restores stable coverage, supporting the gain-scaling mechanism.
card.effect_size_rationale: Gain variations of 20-30% are common and have been shown to cause moderate miscalibration in residual-based conformal methods.
minimum_data_needed: Estimated signal gain per segment (ratio of RMS to baseline)
Residuals from the prediction model per segment
card.testable_prediction: Higher signal gain predicts lower coverage (under-coverage) when using absolute residual scores.
card.failure_condition: No significant relationship between signal gain and coverage error after adjusting for noise level and movement.
card.statistical_test_plan: Linear mixed-effects regression of coverage error on signal gain with random subject intercepts, controlling for baseline noise, movement, filter settings.
card.falsification_test: If normalizing residuals by estimated gain removes the gain-coverage relationship, the mechanism is supported; if the relationship remains, it is falsified.
